【原视频简介】
Bread may seem like one of the simplest foods in the world, but every loaf has its own chemistry, history, and technique behind it. Some rise with wild microorganisms, some puff through trapped steam, and others depend on fermentation, extreme heat, or days of careful preparation.
This video explores major types of bread including sourdough, baguette, naan, pita, rye bread, focaccia, ciabatta, brioche, pretzels, injera, and panettone. 

You’ll discover where each bread originated, how ingredients and baking methods shape its texture and flavor, why some breads develop huge air pockets while others stay dense, and how fermentation, hydration, gluten, steam, and fat change the final loaf. 

We’ll also explore traditional cooking methods, cultural uses, unusual techniques, and the fascinating stories behind breads eaten around the world.

Watch to discover how flour, water, heat, and time can produce completely different breads. Subscribe for more simple and fascinating explanations about food, ingredients, and culinary history.
